item.description:

arXiv:2606.25853v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a model for magnesium-based systems that combines density functional tight binding (DFTB) with MACE, a machine learning interatomic potential (DFTB+MACE). In this model, the conventional repulsive potential, pair potential, is replaced by a many-body MACE potential. The MACE component of the model is trained on the difference between density functional theory (DFT) energies and forces and the corresponding DFTB values, but neglecting the pair potential contribution. Using this model we performed structural relaxation of MgO-CO2 adsorption systems, molecular dynamics calculations of water clusters and phonon spectrum calculations of stable fcc-MgO and metastable bcc-MgO structures. item.title: A machine learning closure for polymer integral equation theory
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
Polymer reference interaction site model (PRISM) theory, a descendant of Ornstein–Zernike liquid state theory, is a powerful tool to predict the structure and thermodynamics of equilibrium polymer systems, but its accuracy and applicability can be limited in some important cases. Typically, these shortcomings are traced to the analytical closure relationships used to solve the integral equations. Here, we propose a machine learning (ML)-based closure relation trained on a dataset of coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of homopolymer melts and solutions. PRISM theory with the ML closure outperforms traditional atomic closures (e.g., Percus–Yevick) in predicting the structure of typical coarse-grained model systems. item.title: Two quantum skyrmions form a magnon Josephson junction
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 R. L. Silva
arXiv:2610.28854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two quantum skyrmions in a frustrated spin-1/2 magnet bind into a molecule, and the molecule acts as a magnon Josephson junction: the relative helicity θ and the number n of magnons transferred between them obey H=E_Cn²⁻Wo̧sθ. DMRG on the J₁₋₋J₂ triangular lattice gives E_C as the curvature of the skyrmion energy at its natural size of seven flipped spins, and the measured helicity coherence fixes Wsimeq0.02J₁, half the skyrmion--antiskyrmion tunnel splitting and independent of the anisotropy. Two helicity qubits side by side are thus strongly coupled by their own interaction.
